title: Serving cache warmup drift classifier and canary policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible evaluation and monitoring pipeline that distinguishes output drift caused by serving cache warmup/prefix reuse from drift caused by model/config changes. Deliver a classifier (thermometer) that tags requests with a confidence score attributing deltas to: (1) cache-assisted token replay, (2) kernel/quantization differences, or (3) model semantics change. Provide telemetry hooks, dashboards, and automated canary gating to block/rollback config/model rollouts when cache-conditioned semantic regression is detected.
acceptance_criteria: A1: End-to-end eval harness that can replay a stratified production workload and produce per-request attribution labels (cache-warm/replay vs model-delta vs unknown)
A2: Delta-classifier with >85% precision at identifying cache-conditioned output shifts on held-out adversarial testsets
A3: Telemetry integration that emits the classifier score and a summary metric (pct cache-conditioned regressions) to Console per-deploy and per-model variant
A4: Canary rollout policy that fails a deployment if cache-conditioned regression fraction exceeds threshold (configurable, default 0.5%)
A5: Runbook and automated remediation: rollback or temporary disable prefix cache for the variant and create a postmortem ticket template
tasks: T1: Design dataset slices (short prompts, long-prefixed convos, system-message sensitive) and synthetic adversarial cases
T2: Implement request-level replay harness that records KV-access trace, exact cache-hit masks, token alignments, and model deterministic outputs
T3: Train a small delta-classifier that uses features: hit-pattern, token-level edit-distance, log-probs delta, kv-cache provenance, and prompt fingerprint
T4: Add telemetry events (classifier_score, hit_fraction, drift_type_tag) to tracing pipeline and Console metrics
T5: Build canary gating rule in rollout service and unit/e2e tests for blocking behavior
T6: Create dashboards and alert rules, document runbook with links to PRs and datasets
